topics: 🗡️ Shema on the Bed — even a scholar says a verse of mercy; a double-edged sword that keeps demons away
⚔️ Inciting the Good Inclination — Reish Lakish's four-stage strategy from Psalm 4:5
🔍 When Suffering Comes — examine your deeds, then suspect neglect of Torah, then afflictions of love
💝 Afflictions of Love — what counts, the covenant of salt, and the three gifts given only through suffering
🤝 'Give Me Your Hand' — Rabbi Yoḥanan at the sickbeds of Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba and Rabbi Elazar, and Rav Huna's 400 barrels
🛏️ Abba Binyamin — prayer near bedtime, a bed set north to south, and waiting for one's fellow in the synagogue

overview.title: 📖 Overview: Afflictions of Love
overview.subtitle: Berakhot 5a–5b
overview.hebrewSource: חֲבִיבִין עָלֶיךָ יִסּוּרִין? לֹא הֵן וְלֹא שְׂכָרָן. הַב לִי יְדָךְ
overview.label: The scene:
overview.text: The daf continues the theme of Shema on one's bed: Abaye requires even a Torah scholar to say at least one verse of mercy, and Rabbi Yitzḥak compares the bedtime Shema to a double-edged sword that keeps demons at bay. Reish Lakish's four-step program for subduing the evil inclination leads into the daf's central subject: suffering. If afflictions come, examine your deeds; if nothing is found, suspect neglect of Torah; if still nothing, these are afflictions of love, which cleanse like salt and through which Torah, Eretz Yisrael, and the World-to-Come are given. Three sickbed scenes with Rabbi Yoḥanan and the story of Rav Huna's soured wine show how the Sages lived these ideas. The daf ends with Abba Binyamin's practices concerning prayer and the bed.

slides.title: ⚔️ Reish Lakish: Four Weapons Against the Evil Inclination
slides.subtitle: Rabbi Levi bar Ḥama in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish, reading Psalm 4:5 phrase by phrase

steps.content: 1️⃣ 'Tremble, and do not sin' (רִגְזוּ וְאַל תֶּחֱטָאוּ) — always incite the good inclination against the evil one. If it wins, good; if not...
2️⃣ 'Say to your heart' (אִמְרוּ בִלְבַבְכֶם) — engage in Torah study. If it wins, good; if not...
3️⃣ 'Upon your bed' (עַל מִשְׁכַּבְכֶם) — recite Shema, accepting the yoke of Heaven and reward and punishment. If it wins, good; if not...
4️⃣ 'And be still, Selah' (וְדֹמּוּ סֶלָה) — remind yourself of the day of death

callout.label: Same teacher, same daf:
callout.text: Reish Lakish also reads Exodus 24:12 — 'the tablets' are the Ten Commandments, 'the Torah' is Scripture, 'the mitzva' is Mishna, 'that I have written' is Prophets and Writings, 'to teach them' is Talmud — teaching that all of these were given to Moses at Sinai. And Rabbi Yitzḥak: one who recites Shema on his bed holds a double-edged sword (Ps. 149:6), and demons keep away from him (Job 5:7).

slides.title: 🔍 If Suffering Comes: Rava's Diagnostic
slides.subtitle: Rava (some say Rav Ḥisda) on how to read one's own afflictions

nodes.content: 😣 A person sees that suffering has come upon him
🔎 Let him examine his deeds — 'Let us search and examine our ways and return to the Lord' (Lam. 3:40)

columns.label: Found a transgression
columns.content: The suffering is punishment for it — and a call to return

columns.label: Found nothing
columns.content: Attribute it to neglect of Torah study (בִּטּוּל תּוֹרָה) — 'Happy is the man whom You afflict, Lord, and teach from Your Torah' (Ps. 94:12)

nodes.content: 💝 Attributed it to neglect of Torah and still found nothing? Then know these are afflictions of love — 'For whom the Lord loves, He rebukes' (Prov. 3:12)

Rav Huna: whom God delights in, He crushes with suffering (Isa. 53:10) — but only if accepted knowingly, like a guilt-offering brought willingly. The reward: 'he shall see offspring, lengthen his days', and his learning endures

callout.label: Rabbi Yoḥanan's warning:
callout.text: One who could study Torah and does not — God brings hideous afflictions that trouble him: 'I was silent from good, and my pain was strong' (Ps. 39:3), and 'good' means Torah (Prov. 4:2). Rabbi Zeira adds: unlike a human seller, God gave Israel the Torah and rejoiced.

slides.title: 💝 What Are 'Afflictions of Love'?
slides.subtitle: Two definitions from a pair of amoraim, then Rabbi Yoḥanan's broader view and his exclusions

boxes.title: No neglect of Torah
items: One of Rabbi Ya'akov bar Idi and Rabbi Aḥa bar Ḥanina
Afflictions of love are those that still allow Torah study
'Happy is the man whom You afflict... and teach from Your Torah' (Ps. 94:12)

boxes.title: No neglect of prayer
items: Afflictions of love are those that still allow one to pray
'Blessed is God Who did not turn away my prayer' (Ps. 66:20)

boxes.title: Rabbi Yoḥanan: both
items: Even afflictions that stop Torah and prayer are of love — 'whom the Lord loves, He rebukes'
Read 'teach him' as 'teach us': the Torah teaches their value a fortiori from a slave freed for a tooth or an eye

But leprosy and children are not afflictions of love — leprosy when visible or in Eretz Yisrael (though still an 'altar of atonement'); children meaning one who has none, for children who died can be afflictions of love

callout.label: Reish Lakish and Rabbi Shimon ben Yoḥai:
callout.text: 'Covenant' is said of salt (Lev. 2:13) and of afflictions (Deut. 28:69): as salt sweetens meat, afflictions cleanse a person's sins. And three good gifts were given to Israel only through suffering — Torah (Ps. 94:12), Eretz Yisrael (Deut. 8:5–7), and the World-to-Come (Prov. 6:23).

slides.title: 🤝 'Is Your Suffering Dear to You?'
slides.subtitle: Three sickbed visits with the same script — and one unexpected reason to weep

lines.speaker: R' Yoḥanan
lines.text: To his sick student Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba: Is your suffering dear to you (חֲבִיבִין עָלֶיךָ יִסּוּרִין)?

lines.speaker: R' Ḥiyya
lines.text: Neither it nor its reward (לֹא הֵן וְלֹא שְׂכָרָן).

lines.speaker: R' Yoḥanan
lines.text: Give me your hand (הַב לִי יְדָךְ). — He gave it, and Rabbi Yoḥanan stood him up.

lines.speaker: Gemara
lines.text: When Rabbi Yoḥanan himself fell ill, Rabbi Ḥanina asked him the same question and raised him. Why could Rabbi Yoḥanan not raise himself? A prisoner cannot free himself from prison (אֵין חָבוּשׁ מַתִּיר עַצְמוֹ מִבֵּית הָאֲסוּרִים).

lines.speaker: R' Yoḥanan
lines.text: Visiting Rabbi Elazar in a dark room, he bared his arm and light filled the house. Seeing him weep: Why cry? If for Torah you did not master — 'one who does much and one who does little' are equal if the heart is directed to Heaven. If for livelihood — not everyone merits two tables. If for children — this is the bone of my tenth son.

lines.speaker: R' Elazar
lines.text: I weep for this beauty of yours that will decay in the earth (לְהַאי שׁוּפְרָא דְּבָלֵי בְּעַפְרָא).

lines.speaker: R' Yoḥanan
lines.text: For that you may certainly weep. — And they both wept. Then: Is your suffering dear to you? Neither it nor its reward. Give me your hand — and he stood him up.

callout.label: Rav Huna's vinegar:
callout.text: Four hundred barrels of Rav Huna's wine soured. The Sages told him to examine his deeds — 'Is God suspected of judging without justice?' They had heard he withheld his tenant farmer's share of the vines. 'He steals everything from me!' 'One who steals from a thief still tastes theft.' He undertook to give the share — and the vinegar turned back into wine, or the price of vinegar rose to that of wine.

slides.title: 🛏️ Abba Binyamin: Prayer, the Bed, and Waiting for a Friend
slides.subtitle: 'All my life I took pains over two things' — and a third teaching about two who enter to pray
rows: 'My prayer should be before my bed'
Not literally in front of the bed — one prays with nothing between himself and the wall, like Hezekiah (Isa. 38:2). Rather: prayer adjacent to going to bed
Rav Yehuda in the name of Rav, or Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi, on facing the wall
'My bed should lie north to south'
The Shekhina rests along the east–west axis of the Temple, so the bed is turned away from that line
Rabbi Yitzḥak: he will have sons — 'whose belly You fill with Your treasure [tzfunekha]' (Ps. 17:14); Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak: his wife will not miscarry (Gen. 25:24)
Two enter to pray; one finishes and leaves the other alone
His prayer is torn up before his face — 'You who tear your soul in your anger' (Job 18:4) — and he causes the Shekhina to depart from Israel: 'the Rock will be moved from its place'
'Rock' is the Holy One (Deut. 32:18). And if he waits for his fellow? The daf ends by asking what his reward is

callout.label: Takeaway:
callout.text: Abba Binyamin's private disciplines — when to pray, how to sleep, and not abandoning a fellow at prayer — all orient daily life toward the Divine Presence.

summary.principle: Suffering is not random: examine your deeds, then your Torah study, and what remains is a covenant of love that cleanses like salt — yet even a sage may say 'neither it nor its reward' and need another's hand to rise.

flowSteps.content: 🗡️ Shema on the bed: even a scholar says a verse of mercy; it is a double-edged sword and drives away demons
⚔️ Reish Lakish: tremble → study Torah → recite Shema → remember the day of death (Ps. 4:5)
🔍 Suffering came? Examine deeds → suspect neglect of Torah → afflictions of love (Prov. 3:12)

columns.content: 💝 The covenant of salt cleanses sins; Torah, the Land, and the World-to-Come come only through suffering
🤝 'Neither it nor its reward' — 'Give me your hand'; a prisoner cannot free himself

flowSteps.content: 🎓 Key Principle: Rav Huna's vinegar turned back to wine once he gave his tenant his due — God does not judge without justice

quiz.q: According to Abaye, what must even a Torah scholar do before sleeping?
o: Recite the entire Shema with its blessings
Recite at least one verse of mercy, such as 'Into Your hand I entrust my spirit'
Study one chapter of Mishna
Recite Psalm 4 in full
quiz.e: The Gemara had said a Torah scholar need not recite Shema on his bed, but Abaye requires him to say at least one verse of prayer for mercy, such as Psalms 31:6.

quiz.q: In Reish Lakish's four-step strategy against the evil inclination, what is the final resort?
o: Fasting
Reciting Shema
Reminding oneself of the day of death
Engaging in Torah study
quiz.e: The order is: incite the good inclination; if that fails, study Torah; if that fails, recite Shema; if that fails, remember the day of death — derived from 'and be still, Selah'.

quiz.q: According to Rava, if a person suffering examines his deeds and finds no transgression, what should he do?
o: Conclude that the suffering is a mistake
Attribute it to neglect of Torah study
Fast until the suffering passes
Ask the Sages to pray on his behalf
quiz.e: Having found no sin, he attributes the suffering to bitul Torah, as in 'Happy is the man whom You afflict, Lord, and teach from Your Torah'. Only if that too does not apply are they afflictions of love.

quiz.q: Why, according to the Gemara, could Rabbi Yoḥanan not heal himself as he healed his students?
o: His own suffering was an affliction of love and had to be endured
A prisoner cannot free himself from prison
He had not accepted his suffering knowingly
Only Rabbi Ḥanina had the power to heal
quiz.e: The Gemara asks why Rabbi Yoḥanan waited for Rabbi Ḥanina and answers with the proverb that a prisoner cannot release himself from prison.

quiz.q: What flaw did the Sages identify when Rav Huna's four hundred barrels of wine turned to vinegar?
o: He had delayed the afternoon prayer
He had not given his tenant farmer his share of the vines
He sold wine at an unfair price
He had not placed his bed north to south
quiz.e: Rav Huna defended himself that the tenant stole from him, but the Sages answered that one who steals from a thief still tastes theft. When he undertook to give the share, his loss was restored.
